title: Monfils wins on 40th birthday as Zverev celebrates at 2am
description: French veteran Gael Monfils is treated to a rendition of Happy Birthday by the US Open crowd as he becomes the oldest man to win a match there since 1992.
fullText:
Most people celebrate their 40th birthday with a slap-up meal or a surprise party.

Gael Monfils, the maverick Frenchman who always knows how to have fun on the court, marked his milestone by winning a Grand Slam match at the US Open.

Playing in the final major of his career, Monfils ensured he had a unforgettable night with a 2-6 6-1 6-2 6-0 victory over Paraguayan opponent Adolfo Daniel Vallejo.

The former world number six is the oldest man to win a US Open main-draw match since Jimmy Connors - who also won on his 40th birthday in 1992.

The New York crowd made the occasion even more memorable for Monfils by bursting into an impromptu rendition of Happy Birthday during his post-victory interview.

"To play on my 40th birthday is very special," said the 2016 US Open semi-finalist, who announced last year he will retire at the end of this season.

"The atmosphere [in New York] is always electric - I feel great here. I always try to play great tennis and put on a great show."

Addressing the thousands of fans who created a celebratory atmosphere on Louis Armstrong Stadium, he added: "You guys rock - let's keep it up for the second round."

No repeat of Wimbledon heroics as Fery exits US Open

Gauff's flaw forgotten on winning US Open return

Rybakina makes winning start in race to number one

Playing in his 18th and final US Open, Monfils made a nervous start against 60th-ranked Vallejo.

However, he quickly settled into the match and dominated the next three sets to secure a 131st Grand Slam match win - extending his all-time record for a Frenchman.

It was a typically entertaining display from the charismatic Monfils, who enthralled the crowd with the stylish shot-making and athleticism for which he is known.

"I didn't want to lose first round, that's for sure," said Monfils, who revealed he was given a watch by his wife Elina Svitolina - the two-time Wimbledon semi-finalist - as a birthday present.

"Somehow I felt like even with a sloppy start, I could do better. I kept going for my shots, being versatile with my backhand, tried to use my forehand.

"My rhythm was there and then I had this feeling where I can be in cruise control."

Monfils will continue his farewell appearance at Flushing Meadows against American 14th seed Learner Tien.

One man also left celebrating in the early hours of the New York morning was top seed Alexander Zverev.

The 29-year-old German survived a huge scare against Italy's Lorenzo Sonego to win a five-set thriller at almost 2am on Arthur Ashe Stadium.

Zverev is aiming to reach the final for the third successive Grand Slam, but almost fell at the first hurdle after being pushed to the limit by 89th-ranked Sonego for almost five hours.

Sonego, 31, produced a stunning performance to lead by two sets to one - and was two points away from victory in the fourth set.

But Zverev, who won the first major of his career at the French Open before reaching the Wimbledon final, showed great resolve to escape with a 6-4 3-6 6-7 (7-9) 7-5 6-4 victory.

"I'm just happy I won - that's it," said Zverev.

"It was an incredible battle with ups and downs. I think it's the longest first round match I've ever played in my life.

"He played amazing tennis and would have beaten a lot of players for sure."

With world number one Jannik Sinner missing through injury, 29-year-old Zverev leads the seedings at a major for the first time in his career.

His prospects also appear to have been aided by Spanish second seed Carlos Alcaraz's lack of match practice following a long-term wrist injury, as well as 24-time major champion Novak Djokovic's own first-round exit on Sunday.

But with that increased sense of opportunity seemed to come edginess against Sonego.

Zverev, who suffered early exits in Montreal and Cincinnati leading into the US Open, was well below his best again as Sonego threatened to further blow open the men's singles draw.

"This was exactly the sort of match I needed," said Zverev, who goes on to play France's Quentin Halys in the second round.

"I struggled in the last two tournaments, I didn't play well and sometimes good things happen after you fight through one of these matches."

title: Trump says he's nominating acting Navy Secretary Hung Cao for the permanent job
description: President Donald Trump said Tuesday that he is nominating acting Navy Secretary Hung Cao for the permanent job, giving the Navy combat veteran the nod as concerns have emerged that some sailors have b...
fullText:
WASHINGTON (AP) — President Donald Trump said Tuesday that he is nominating acting Navy Secretary Hung Cao for the permanent job, giving the Navy combat veteran the nod as concerns have emerged that some sailors have been stretched to the limit during the Iran war.

Cao has been serving as acting Navy secretary since John Phelan departed the job unexpectedly and without explanation in late April. Unlike Phelan, who had not served in the military or had a civilian leadership role in the service, Cao spent 25 years in the Navy as a special operations officer and went on to serve with SEAL teams and special forces in Iraq and Afghanistan.

"I am pleased to nominate a true WARRIOR," Trump wrote on social media, prodding the Senate "to confirm this Warfighter, ASAP."

Cao on social media called it the "honor of a lifetime to lead the great warriors of the Navy and Marine Corps team."

Cao's nomination comes as some, including Democrats in Congress, believe Trump has been overtaxing the Navy. The USS Abraham Lincoln aircraft carrier's nine-month deployment to support the Iran war has included a record-setting uninterrupted time at sea.

Concerns grew about the Lincoln's deployment following reports of deteriorating mental health among the crew and shortages of supplies including food and hygiene products. Several Democratic lawmakers, including Sens. Richard Blumenthal of Connecticut and Ruben Gallego of Arizona, are pressing for accountability from the Pentagon over conditions aboard the ship.

Cao served as Navy undersecretary before his current role. He championed returning to duty service members who refused a Biden-era mandate to take the COVID-19 vaccine. The Trump loyalist also said he had no problem with the Navy's demonstration squadron, the Blue Angels, flying so low over a crowded Florida beach in July that chairs and tents went flying.

Cao's nomination also comes at a time of upheaval in the top ranks of the U.S. military. In the latest example, Army Secretary Dan Driscoll submitted his resignation this week amid widespread reports of tension between him and Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth.

title: Steelers GM confirms Max Hurleman, Lew Nichols and more practice squad signings
description: The Steelers kept all 10 of their NFL draft picks on the initial 53-man roster, forcing some demotions for some veteran players.
fullText:
More than a dozen players who practiced and played with the Pittsburgh Steelers during training camp and the preseason will be sticking around.

GM Omar Khan confirmed a list of 13 players signed to the team's practice squad as of the afternoon of Monday, Aug. 31.

It includes: Running backs Lew Nichols and Travis Homer; receivers Max Hurleman and Brandon Smith; tight end Lake McRee; offensive linemen Doug Nester and Steven Jones; defensive linemen Esezi Otomewo and Kyler Baugh; cornerback Doneiko Slaughter; safety Sebastian Castro; and linebackers Jacoby Windmon and Julius Welschof.

Required reading: Steelers keep both Drew Allar, Will Howard behind Aaron Rodgers, Mason Rudolph at QB

The Steelers cut all of them from the active roster ahead of the NFL's Sunday deadline to reduce roster sizes to the standard 53 players. The team can still add up to four more names to the practice squad before finalizing the group ahead of Week 1, when they face the Atlanta Falcons on Sept. 13 at Acrisure Stadium. They will get an exemption for an extra spot because Welschof is an international pathway player.

Nicols and Homer led the backfield in two of three preseason games but were squeezed out of the active roster by rookie Eli Heidenreich, the team's seventh-round selection who also has utility on special teams. He'll be the lone backup behind top backs Jaylen Warren and Rico Dowdle for now.

Hurleman was a standout with 99 total receiving yards through the three contests against the Green Bay Packers, New York Jets and Buffalo Bills. He gave way to rookie Kaden Wetjen, who's the lead kick returner on special teams, as well as Ben Skowronek, a Pro Bowl selection for his special teams play last season.

McRee opened some eyes working mostly with the backup quarterbacks. He caught a 38-yard pass from Drew Allar in the loss to the Jets on Aug. 21, then added a touchdown from Will Howard in the finale.

Defensively, Welschof had two sacks in the exhibition campaign.

Injuries will be the main factor in any of these players getting called up to the active roster at some point this season. Hurleman, Hurleman and Nichols would be most likely to earn promotions if rookies like Heidenreich and Wetjen struggle to find their footing.

title: Phillies Trade Veteran Outfielder To White Sox

Pham has spent time with the New York Mets and Baltimore Orioles this season as well. The Phillies signed him to a minor league deal in June, and since he was not called up to the big leagues after that, he is eligible to be traded despite the trade deadline having passed.

Pham is being acquired prior to Sept. 1, so he is postseason eligible. The White Sox have actually done the unthinkable and are expected to be playing baseball in October. In fact, if the season ended today, they would have a bye.

Pham is expected to be activated to the active roster when rosters expand on Tuesday. He has played in nine games in the big leagues this year, all with the Mets. He went hitless in those nine games. However, he has a .775 OPS in the minor leagues this year.

Buffalo announced their roster cuts on Sunday evening, and one of the notable cuts was veteran wide receiver Trent Sherfield. The Bills brought back Sherfield on a one-year deal, and he was competing for a roster spot, but obviously didn't do enough.

Sherfield, meanwhile, said after getting cut by the Broncos, his perspective on his future changed.

"A lot of people get cut. Top guys get released all the time and I think it's just a perspective change," Sherfield said. "… My perspective has changed a lot. … I just told myself that I wasn't going to allow my career to end like that. title: Patriots Work Out Veteran Specialist Amid Punter Uncertainty
description: New England reportedly evaluated another experienced option after an injury created sudden uncertainty at punter.
fullText:
Patriots Work Out Veteran Specialist Amid Punter Uncertainty originally appeared on NESN. 

The New England Patriots are exploring another potential solution to their unexpected uncertainty at punter. New England worked out veteran Jamie Gillan on Thursday, according to the NFL transaction wire, as first noted by Pats Pulpit. The visit came before the Patriots closed their preseason schedule against the Cleveland Browns, the team Gillan began his NFL career with in 2019.

Gillan's workout was notable because Bryce Baringer suffered an injury during New England's second preseason game. The Patriots already signed veteran Matt Haack to provide immediate depth, but their interest in Gillan showed they were continuing to examine the available options. Baringer's absence created an unusual scene against the Philadelphia Eagles. Rookie quarterback Behren Morton was forced to handle a punt after Baringer left the game.

New England understandably did not want to repeat that situation.

MORE: Patriots Star A.J. Brown, Wife Announce Exciting Family News

Gillan, nicknamed "The Scottish Hammer," has appeared in 107 NFL games across six seasons.

The 29-year-old signed with Cleveland as an undrafted free agent out of Arkansas-Pine Bluff in 2019. He earned AFC Special Teams Player of the Week, AFC Special Teams Player of the Month and PFWA All-Rookie honors during his first season. Gillan spent three years with the Browns before briefly joining the Buffalo Bills' practice squad. He then served as the New York Giants' punter from 2022 through the 2025 season before being released in March.

The Scotland native has averaged 45.2 yards per punt and 40.3 net yards per punt during his career. His longest attempt traveled 74 yards, and 162 of his 436 punts have been downed inside the opponent's 20-yard line. Gillan also is a left-footed punter, which could provide New England with a different option if Baringer is not ready for the beginning of the regular season.

Haack remains the more immediate answer. The well-traveled veteran has played for the Miami Dolphins, Bills, Indianapolis Colts, Browns and Giants. His experience as both a punter and holder made him a sensible late-preseason addition. Working out Gillan does not guarantee the Patriots will sign him. NFL teams routinely evaluate free agents to update their emergency lists, particularly around the roster reduction deadline.

The visit nevertheless confirmed that New England was not leaving anything to chance.

The Patriots entered the summer expecting Baringer to handle their punting duties. His injury forced them to adjust quickly, and Gillan now represents another experienced option if the uncertainty continues into the regular season.

title: Chargers player lands on chopping block among veterans ahead of cuts
description: This Chargers veteran offensive lineman is among the potential players who could be cut before the 53-man rosters are finalized.
fullText:
The Chargers are a few weeks away from the start of what should be an exciting and thrilling 2026 season.

Los Angeles has set itself up for a great season and should be in the thick of things in the AFC West and the conference. However, before all that takes place, the Chargers will cut down their roster from 90 players to 53.

That is all set to take place on August 30, and there will be some tough decisions to make from now until then. Usually, undrafted young players or fringe NFL guys get cut more often than not; however, veteran offensive lineman Trevor Penning is a prime candidate for the chopping block.

Carter Bahns of CBS Sports listed 20 veterans who could be cut, and Penning was among them.

"Los Angeles' maligned offensive line is now mostly healthy and rebuilt, so there is less need for Penning, who would be nothing more than a second-teamer if he stuck on the roster. Considering all it cost to get him was a sixth-round pick, the Chargers can easily cut bait."

Penning is a former first-round pick in 2022 by the Saints and spent the 2025 season with the Chargers. The 27-year-old re-signed with the Bolts on a one-year deal in March 2026.

It's been tough for Penning in Los Angeles due to a variety of reasons. For starters, he has struggled with pass protection, frequent penalties, and adjusting to multiple position shifts on an injury-depleted offensive line.

The Chargers' offensive line has plenty of questions entering the season, especially after losing center Tyler Biadasz. The uncertainty doesn't stop there, as the interior offensive line remains unsettled.

Even so, there's a chance Penning will look for a new team by next week.

title: Nike brought back a 32-year veteran to save the $60B brand. Two years later, its turnaround is still a ‘long, hard slog’
description: CEO Elliott Hill has started fixing Nike’s business. Winning back the consumers and cultural cachet it lost could be much harder.
fullText:
The news traveled quickly across Nike's sprawling headquarters in Beaverton, Ore. Elliott Hill was coming back.

Employees high-fived. An audible cheer could be heard in parts of Nike's 400-acre campus. Current and former employees lit up group chats and social media. On Wall Street, investors joined the celebration, sending Nike shares up roughly 8% in after-hours trading following the company's September 2024 announcement that Hill would come out of retirement to replace John Donahoe as chief executive.

Can Nike regain relevance with younger generation consumers?

What cultural challenges is Nike facing with consumers?

How has Elliott Hill's Nike turnaround performed so far?

The exuberance reflected more than relief that Donahoe was leaving. Hill's return carried an almost messianic quality inside a company that had spent several years watching its innovation pipeline sputter, relationships with retailers deteriorate, and its once-untouchable cultural standing erode. Nike was reaching into its own past for someone who seemed uniquely equipped to restore what it had lost.

Hill had spent over 32 years at Nike, rising from an intern in 1988 through sales and leadership positions across North America and Europe before eventually becoming president of consumer and marketplace. By the time he retired in 2020, Nike credited him with helping grow the business to some $39 billion.

The appeal to Nike's board was obvious. It was buying a turnaround CEO and, just as importantly, buying time. Hill would not have to spend his first year learning the company he had been hired to save. He knew how Nike worked when it was working. He presumably knew where it had gone wrong.

Nearly two years later, the savior narrative has collided with the scale of Nike's problems.

Hill has repaired relationships with wholesalers, curbed the flood of once-hot sneaker styles Nike let saturate the retail market, and poured resources back into athletic innovation. Wholesale has returned to growth, and performance running is showing signs of renewed strength.

Still, investors remain unconvinced, and the stock market's initial euphoria has long since disappeared. Nike shares, which jumped when Hill's appointment was announced, now trade around $40, roughly half their 52-week high and a fraction of their 2021 peak. The decline has reduced Nike to the lowest-priced member of the price-weighted Dow Jones Industrial Average and generated speculation about whether the company could eventually lose its place in the index, an extraordinary symbolic comedown for a brand that once seemed synonymous with American consumer dominance.

"The initial excitement around the appointment has been replaced by a realization that this is a long, hard slog," says Neil Saunders, managing director at GlobalData Retail. "There are no real quick fixes here."

title: Lindsay Clancy trial: Postpartum is real, but child killing demands accountability, veteran prosecutor says
description: Veteran child abuse prosecutor Jonathan Hatami says public support for Lindsay Clancy is overshadowing the three children she is accused of killing.
fullText:

While failures by people, medical professionals and systems around Lindsay Clancy deserve scrutiny, nothing should erase a parent's responsibility for killing a child, according to a veteran prosecutor who said he's concerned that public support for the Massachusetts mom is overshadowing the killing of her three young children.

Clancy is accused of killing her three young children — Cora, 5, Dawson, 3, and Callan, 8 months — and trying to end her own life by dropping from a second-floor window after sending her husband to pick up takeout and something from a pharmacy, according to the Plymouth County District Attorney's Office.

But as the case has drawn national attention, Clancy has also attracted supporters both online and in-person at the courthouse, and experts have warned that that support has taken attention away from the victims.

"Nobody who murders children is a victim no matter what they're suffering through," said Jonathan Hatami, a veteran child abuse prosecutor. "You're never a victim if you murder people because victims don't do something. Something happens to them."

The defense does not dispute that Clancy caused the deaths — but she has pleaded not guilty and is contesting criminal responsibility.

Hatami has spearheaded a number of high-profile cases against child abusers in Los Angeles, California, including the murder of 8-year-old Gabriel Fernandez, who was tortured and killed by his mother and her boyfriend. Gabriel's killing exposed a series of missed red flags by the county's Department of Children and Family Services and inspired a Netflix docuseries.

"Gabriel Fernandez was tortured and murdered by his mom and her boyfriend — however, there were a lot of other people...that were responsible," Hatami told Fox News Digital. "There were a lot of people that missed signs through the eight or nine months of Gabriel's torture. There were a lot of people in government, in law enforcement, social workers, who missed all these different signs that really could have saved Gabriel — and they didn't do it. However, Pearl Fernandez and Isauro Aguirre were ultimately responsible for the torture and murder of Gabriel and were prosecuted for that and they were convicted of that."

In Clancy's case, he argued, many of the people and systems around her deserve scrutiny — but that should not turn her into the central victim of the story. In his view, she's been too much of the focus.

"Instead of about the three victims who were innocent kids," he said.

While failures of government and the child welfare system were investigated after Gabriel's murder, that didn't take responsibility away from the killers, he said. And in the Clancy case, he said he sees a risk that the focus on her mental health could eclipse the three children who were killed in their own home.

"I didn't see people out in the streets cheering on Pearl Fernandez because there were other people that were somewhat responsible for what happened to Gabriel," he said. "And the same thing plays in this case. Lindsay admitted to strangling her three children to death. She admitted to strangling them to death with exercise cords."

Clancy's defense has said she sought help repeatedly as she struggled with depression, sleeplessness, suicidal thoughts and voices urging her to harm herself and the children.

Defense attorney Kevin Reddington has argued that Clancy was under the effects of postpartum psychosis, while prosecutors allege she acted deliberately and understood what she was doing was wrong.

"If you murder your children, you need to be held accountable and responsible for that," Hatami said. "No matter what the whys are, no matter what reasons are."

If convicted of any of the three counts of first-degree murder she faces, Clancy would see a sentence of life in prison without the possibility of parole.

The two-time Cy Young winner has fully embraced the moniker handed to him by veteran infielder Miguel Rojas, and he couldn't be happier about it.

Speaking to reporters after Saturday's win over the Pittsburgh Pirates, Skubal explained the origins of the playful nickname with a grin.

"It's great. I think it's funny, you know, lighthearted," he told reporters after the game. "He's really good at those types of things with everybody on the team. Everyone kind of has their own unique thing."

title: Auburn Offensive Line Showing Encouraging Signs Ahead of Baylor
description: Auburn offensive lineman Jo Simmons believes the Tigers have made significant progress up front entering the 2026 season. With improved continuity, veteran experience and daily battles against Jared Smith and Darrion Smith, Auburn's rebuilt offensive line is beginning to take shape ahead of Week 1 a
fullText:
Jo Simmons has played a lot of college football.

And he likes what he's starting to see from the Auburn Tigers offensive line.

The Tigers are two weeks away from putting their full attention on the field in Atlanta against the Baylor Bears, but Simmons believes the biggest difference from spring to fall camp isn't necessarily one individual player. It's how Auburn's offensive line has started to gel together and find continuity despite the position battles.

"We've definitely taken big steps this summer, like continuity and just playing next to each other and just spending time with each other," Simmons said on a recent interview with The Top Button podcast.

And with everything new coming to the planes in 2026, that seems pretty important.

Auburn entered the offseason needing to rebuild its offensive line, and competitions are still happening throughout the group. Deryk Plazz and Jacob Strand have rotated at left guard next to Simmons, while Stanton Ramil's return has given Auburn another experienced player at tackle.

Having two players with that type of experience anchoring the offensive line is something that Simmons deems very important.

"There's so much savvy thing you could do as like an older guy that like helps you, and it's hard to get that experience without actually playing games," Simmons said.

While Alex Golesh and the rest of the Auburn offensive coaching staff continue to figure out who the five will be on the first snap of offense against the Baylor Bears, the offensive linemen are getting plenty of help from the other side of the football.

On the defense at the trenches, Simmons specifically mentioned two Auburn defenders who have made life difficult during fall camp.

"For as big as he is, he's athletic as ever, and he could get off the ball," Simmons said.

Smith is a player who needs to take a huge step forward in 2026 because the DJ Durkin defense is relying on him. He is seen as the top edge rusher entering the season. If he can bring pressure to opponents' quarterbacks and allow the rest of the defense to flow freely, he truly has an opportunity to make an impact on every game as well as Auburn's win-loss total.

Then there's Darrion Smith, who is another example of a sophomore continuing to receive praise from just about everyone following the last few scrimmages.

"D Smith is like, he's been balling, man," Simmons said. "He's twitched up and like he's been all over the line."

For the first time in what feels like half a decade, the Auburn offense has competed in a good way against the Auburn defense in practice. The fact that they have challenged the other side shows a different direction that Alex Golesh has already decided to go, establishing a new standard on the Plains.

Simmons believes the Tigers have enough talent to make this thing work. Now it's about Auburn's coaching staff getting the most out of it. Players such as Byrum Brown do not want this year to be seen as a year where Auburn is only building up and establishing their identity. They want to be competitive right away.

"The talent was already there," Simmons said. "You just need someone to actually put them in the right spots."

Auburn fans will get a first taste of what this offensive line will look like in Atlanta in Week 1.

title: Nick Bolton on the impact of two veteran players during training camp

title: Veteran Dem defeats scandal-plagued former lawmaker, progressive challenger in Trump's backyard
description: Debbie Wasserman Schultz faced a progressive challenger and fraud-accused ex-lawmaker in Florida's 20th Congressional District Democratic primary.
fullText:
Rep. Debbie Wasserman Schultz has bested a young progressive challenger and an embattled former lawmaker after a hard-fought primary characterized by its racial overtones.

Schultz, a 21-year veteran of the House, stressed her seniority on the campaign trail and her ability to deliver services to constituents and secure federal funding for her district.

To secure her primary victory, Schultz defeated former Rep. Sheila Cherfilus-McCormick, who resigned in April following fraud allegations, and 27-year-old activist and teacher Elijah Manley, who is aligned with the progressive wing of the Democratic Party.

Jeffries Declines To Back Wasserman Schultz As Black Leaders Revolt Over District Switch

Mid-decade redistricting in Florida prompted Schultz to choose to run in Florida's 20th Congressional District, which has a stronger Democratic lean than her home constituency.

Schultz, a White woman, drew considerable backlash for deciding to run in the district in May. Criticism centered around the district being majority Black and having long been represented by a Black member of Congress.

Both Cherfilus-McCormick and Manley argued that Schultz representing Florida's 20th Congressional District would be an affront to the African American community. House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries declined to back Schultz during the dispute.

"While the Republicans are trying their hardest to silence Black voices, I don't expect somebody in our own party, a White Democrat, to do the same," Manley said of Schultz at a candidate debate. "We are not going back to a time where there were no Black people in Congress."

Tlaib Under Fire For Working To Unseat Two Jewish House Democrats In Florida: 'No Coincidence'

Cherfilus-McCormick accused Schultz of "district forum shopping" and said electing her would amount to the erasure of Black history and power.

During a debate, Schultz defended her candidacy by emphasizing her extensive tenure in Congress and her experience representing Black and Caribbean communities in her former district.

Cherfilus-McCormick's candidacy was itself mired in controversy.

Federal prosecutors say Cherfilus-McCormick and her co-defendants stole a $5 million overpayment from a FEMA-funded COVID-19 vaccination contract, laundered the money through multiple accounts and used part of it to finance her 2021 congressional campaign through illegal contributions. She resigned from Congress in April before an expulsion vote could be scheduled and has pleaded not guilty to the federal charges.

Former Bernie Sanders Official Accuses Senator Of Pushing Most Antisemitic Candidates 'In A Generation'

Accusations that Schultz was carpetbagging and the federal fraud charges against Cherfilus-McCormick weren't the only controversies in the Democratic primary in Florida's 20th Congressional District.

Rep. Rashida Tlaib appeared at a Fort Lauderdale Chomp the Oligarchy rally Aug. 14 to support the effort to oust Schultz from Congress. Rep. Randy Fine, R-Fla., has claimed the effort to oust Schultz stems from the fact that she is Jewish.

Schultz has described herself as a "staunch supporter" of Israel and has voted against measures to cut off military aid. Her position has put her at odds with progressives seeking to reduce U.S. support for Israel.

Other candidates in the Democratic primary for Florida's 20th Congressional District included former Broward County Mayor Dale Holness and longtime community activist Luther "Uncle Luke" Campbell.

title: Manhunt underway after off-duty Massachusetts police veteran found dead at woman's home

An urgent manhunt is underway in Massachusetts for a 58-year-old woman who police warn may be armed after a Worcester police officer was found dead at her home.

The Worcester Police Department said in an alert that officers are actively seeking Karen Solomon "regarding the death of a male at her residence."

Police described her as a 58-year-old White woman with dark brown hair and brown eyes last seen wearing pajama shorts and a tank top and walking toward Westcott Street.

New York State Police Launch Manhunt After Killing, House Fire For 'Armed And Dangerous' Suspect

"There is concern she may be armed," the department said. Police have not publicly identified the man or said how he died.

Police said the officer found dead was a 30-year veteran of the force and was off duty at the time he was found.

The officer who died has been identified as 31-year Worcester Police Department veteran Kurt Solomon, according to the New England Police Benevolent Association.

The NEPBA announced Solomon's death Tuesday, remembering him as an "incredibly dependable officer, colleague and friend" who dedicated more than three decades to serving the Worcester community.

The association said the investigation into the circumstances surrounding Solomon's death remains active and that authorities are working to locate the individual being sought.

Solomon is survived by his sons, Niklas and Brandon; his mother, Shirley; and his brothers, Karl and Eric, according to the NEPBA.

CBS Boston reported that Massachusetts State Police were searching the area with a helicopter and that a special emergency response team was being brought in to search nearby woods. Fox News has reached out to authorities for confirmation and additional details.

Solomon's home is on Wildwood Avenue, where authorities are conducting the death investigation, according to CBS Boston. The outlet also reported that Solomon said in a 2016 interview that she was married to a Worcester police officer and had made telling the stories of law enforcement a personal mission.

Solomon told WBZ-TV at the time that she was inspired to write "Hearts Beneath The Badge" after her son came home from school and asked why someone had told him that police "kill people for no reason." Solomon said she wanted to highlight the good deeds officers perform, from buying meals to saving lives and putting themselves in danger for others.

She later wrote "The Price They Pay," which focused on what she described as the darker side of policing, including the pain and anxiety officers can experience on the job.

Solomon also developed 1stHelp.Net, a website designed to connect first responders experiencing mental, physical or financial crises with resources. She told WBZ-TV that many officers she interviewed did not know where to seek help or were afraid to do so.

Neighbors told CBS Boston they were stunned by the developments. One resident described the officer as an "awesome guy" who he regularly saw walking around the neighborhood.

Police urged members of the public who spot Solomon not to approach her and to immediately contact authorities.

Anyone with information is asked to call the Worcester Police Department at 508-799-8606 or dial 911 in an emergency.

Fox News Digital reached out to the Worcester District Attorney's Office, Massachusetts State Police and Worcester Police Department for comment but did not immediately receive a response.

title: Opinion - No, the troops aren’t mentally weak. They just have terrible leadership.
description: Marine veteran Joslin Joseph criticizes the leadership of President Trump and Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth for prioritizing mission goals over troop welfare during an ongoing conflict with Iran.
fullText:
"Mission Accomplishment always comes before Troop Welfare." This mantra was drilled into me as a junior enlisted Marine and has stayed with me well into my career spanning professional sports, project management, and now as a writer. The premise is very simple. You always have to make sure that you focus on completing the mission. No matter if it's a life-or-death battle or something as pedestrian as a corporate product release.

You will have subordinates who always come up with plenty of needs, asks, excuses and problems that they need to deal with. They may have personal problems, financial issues, workplace conflicts, or just have lost motivation to work. And while you deal with all that, you must make sure that you are keeping an eye on the prize and getting you and your team to get the job done. This might make you the bad guy, but let's be honest. If you don't get the mission accomplished, you failed.

However, there is one major corollary to this mantra. Yes, mission accomplishment always comes before troop welfare. But if you aren't taking care of your troops, the chance of your mission succeeding drops substantially. Plenty of military leaders (and business leaders too) have always focused on the first part and completely ignored the second part to disastrous effects.

Enter the USS Abraham Lincoln. Reports of sailors and Marines tasked to the limit on a never ending deployment, plumbing issues, food shortages, and most damningly, being stuck in a combat zone for a war that we have won multiple times according to their commander-in-chief. If you were tuned into military circles, the rumors of terrible morale had abounded since a fire in the laundry room of another carrier, the USS Gerald Ford, broke out and forced that carrier into repairs.

But instead of coming home, President Trump, Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth, and what it's turning out to be a horde of yes-men in the Pentagon's upper civilian circle disregarded military leaders concerns of extended deployments, military readiness, manpower shortages, and the logistics of carrying out an offensive/naval blockade/missile defense/whatever Trump decides helps the stock market military operation against Iran.

Trump proving that he is not the military genius or beloved commander he makes himself out to be seemingly doubled down on the situation saying that their deployment wasn't long enough. Hegseth, a middle of the road military officer, has said that the pictures, news reports, and actual testimonies from the troops were misrepresented.

There is no doubt that the war with Iran that most Americans did not want is going poorly. But it takes a special type of incompetence to be the leader of a military and have a lack of awareness for how badly that affects morale.

Trump has long and rightfully been criticized for his lack of understanding of the sacrifice of military members. His disrespect for military awards, calling the war dead suckers and losers, and fudging the numbers of the war dead from the Iran conflict all stem from the fact that he views them as props.

When he needs a photo op, the troops are valuable to him. When he needs to give a State of the Union address and distract from the fact that the state of the union is terrible, he will march out soldiers and give them medals. A man who has mastered the art of social media deception learned that performative stunts like hugging flags, giving a thumbs up while standing on a grave in Arlington, or saluting a dead soldier in a Trump merch hat somehow convinces people that he actually cares.

But we are at war and the performance theatre of both Trump and Hegseth has gotten stale. We care about our troops being in harm's way and want them not just to be safe, but to be cared for. Military life isn't easy and no one is asking for these troops to be coddled. The troops themselves don't want to be coddled.

We will hear from the toxic vet-bro culture that these issues pale in comparison to what they did back in the day. We will get the veteran pissing contests that sound a lot like how your parents told you about how they walked to school. I have my own stories to tell. But I am also of the type of veteran to know that because I suffered, doesn't mean the people after me have to deal with stupid stuff too. Especially if it could be avoided.

Of course, we forget that Bob Hope didn't do USO Tours to look good for the public. It was because he knew how it affected soldiers to be away from home. There is a reason why mail delivery was important to locations as far away as Guadalcanal. There is a reason why we modernized our food preparation (thank you Chef Boyardee) to make sure troops were well fed. There is a reason why I got hundreds of letters from total strangers while I was in Iraq (I still have all of them).

Trump, Hegseth and their associates sold Americans on making the military more lethal. Instead, they started another forever war and stuck thousands of troops in the worst kind of stress with no support or relief. They forgot that taking care of troop welfare means a better chance of mission success. Or maybe they aren't good enough leaders to have known that in the first place.

Joslin Joseph is a recipient of the Military Reporters and Editors award for Best Commentary / Opinion. A graduate of Harvard and Ohio State, he is a Marine veteran who served in Iraq. He currently lives in Anaheim, Calif.

The former All-Pro entered training camp attempting to establish himself as an important piece of Minnesota's secondary. His physical playing style and ability to contribute near the line of scrimmage gave the Vikings another potential weapon defensively.

Now Minnesota must move forward without him.

Losing Adams before the regular season begins creates another decision for the Vikings as they evaluate their safety depth and determine how to replace the snaps Adams was expected to receive.

Preseason games are designed to help teams answer roster questions, but Minnesota left Saturday night facing one it never wanted.

fullText:
PEREIRA, Colombia, Aug 13 (Reuters) - With his lean, sinewy frame, and standing just over 5 feet (1.6 meters) ‌tall, Julio Cesar Pineda feels he was destined for the ‌work of burrowing into the debris of shattered buildings to find survivors — first ​when a quake hit his native Colombia in 1999, and again just this week.

His efforts have won him a nickname: "Rescate" ('Rescue').

When Monday's 7.4-magnitude earthquake pummeled western Colombia, the 67-year-old was at home, near the city of ‌Pereira, in the country's ⁠coffee-growing region that was close to the epicenter of the disaster. A wall in his house collapsed, ⁠but Pineda was unhurt and decided to help those who might have been less fortunate.

"All I did was grab some gloves ... grab a ​helmet, and ​go save lives," Pineda told Reuters.

title: 'Big Short' investor Steve Eisman says Anthropic and OpenAI are the 'Achilles' heel' of the AI trade
description: The veteran of the 2008 market crash is concerned that the success so many companies is reliant on the fortunes of just two AI labs.
fullText:
Steve Eisman is worried that success of the AI trade relies on just two companies: OpenAI and Anthropic.

The famed investor warns of risks to the broader AI ecosystem if they were to run into trouble.

A price war with cheaper Chinese models would be a problem for OpenAI and Anthropic, he says.

The market is eagerly awaiting the day when OpenAI and Anthropic go public, but to Steve Eisman, the two AI giants are the soft underbelly of the AI trade.

Anthropic is barreling toward an IPO that could surpass this summer's historic SpaceX offering by valuation and by funds raised. Reports of a $2 trillion valuation would vault the Claude maker into the ranks of the world's most valuable companies.

But Steve Eisman, the trader whose contrarian bets against the housing market were chronicled in "The Big Short," is worried that too much of the AI trade is reliant on the success of just two companies.

"The 'Achilles' heel' of this whole story, if there's going to be an Achilles' heel, is if something bad happens to Anthropic and OpenAI," Eisman told CNBC, warning of a potential price war if cheaper models from China start to take market share. "And then we have a problem."

After years of powering stocks to new highs, the AI trade has proven to be a market-driving force yet again in 2026, concerns about the sustainability of the investment boom continue to grow.

"The issue is, to me, that something like 70% of all AI revenue from Microsoft, Amazon, Google, Oracle is from Anthropic and OpenAI. Period. Just those two…The futures of these massive companies, in a sense, are a bet that OpenAI Anthropic are going to succeed."

Eisman isn't the first to raise concerns about the finances of the two AI giants. Researcher and independent journalist Ed Zitron warned earlier this summer that OpenAI could end up being the Lehman Brothers of the AI trade, a systemic risk that takes down other companies if it were to stumble.

Meanwhile, the rise of the open-weight Chinese models, such as Kimi K3, caused panic on Wall Street last month as chip stocks fell on fears greater competition in the AI market. But as with DeepSeek's roll out in January 2025, the losses have mostly been recovered and the jitters have subsisded. The Philadelphia Semiconductor Index is up 75% year to date.

Despite his concerns, Eisman clarified that he's not willing to make a call on a price war between OpenAI and Anthropic and their Chinese rivals yet, at least not until investors have more information about both companies' finances.

"It'll be nice when Anthropic goes public, so we can see real numbers and then see every quarter how they're doing," he stated. "Until then, it's just anecdotal."

title: Watch: Freddie Freeman falls down Royals dugout steps, Dodgers 'dodge' bullet
description: Los Angeles Dodgers veteran Freddie Freeman fell down dugout steps, resulting in soreness throughout his body in a win over the Kansas City Royals.
fullText:
Aug. 13 (UPI) -- Los Angeles Dodgers veteran Freddie Freeman fell down dugout steps, resulting in soreness throughout his body in a win over the Kansas City Royals.

The tumble occurred in the top of the eighth inning of the 4-2 victory Wednesday in Los Angeles. Freeman said he felt soreness in his knees, shoulder, hand and wrist, but did not break any bones.

"I didn't hit my head, so that was the key part," Freeman told reporters.

Freeman said he used the cold tub and was in "good spirits" during his postgame news conference. He said he is hopeful to play Thursday at Dodger Stadium.

"I'm OK," said Freeman, who said everything on his right side is sore. "This one's not my ankle, so I should be OK."

The 10-time All-Star went 1 for 2 with a walk and a strikeout in the win. The Dodgers trailed twice through the first 2 1/2 innings, with the Royals taking two one-run leads. They took a 3-2 edge off a 397-foot, two-run homer from Shohei Ohtani and never looked back. Catcher Hunter Feduccia provided insurance with a 402-foot solo shot in the fourth.

Royals pinch hitter John Rave started the eighth with a fly out to right fielder Kyle Tucker. Designated hitter Carter Jensen reached base through a fielding error in the next at-bat.

Left fielder Isaac Collins then walked to the plate with two outs. He earned a 2-1 lead in the count against Dodgers relief pitcher Landon Knack. The right-handed pitcher then tossed in a 93-mph fastball, which Collins sliced into foul territory near first base.

Freeman pursued the ball and hovered toward the dugout. He then took a long step with his left foot, but fell down the steps instead of snagging the final out of the inning. The Dodgers star, who said he was attempting to lean on the dugout fence, told reporters that he misjudged its location. Royals players and coaches checked on Freeman before he got up and left the dugout.

Pinch hitter Michal Massey struck out in the next exchange, ending the half inning.

Freeman, who was set to lead off the bottom of the eighth, was replaced by Tommy Edman. The 17-year veteran said he experienced a similar fall about 10 years ago.

"I think that we really dodged a bullet," Dodgers manager Dave Roberts said. "Very scary visually. ... For right now, he's in good spirits, which I think is a good sign. Just kind of total body soreness. He'll be day-to-day."

Shohei flips the script! pic.twitter.com/eVrqvcBmMs— Los Angeles Dodgers (@Dodgers) August 13, 2026

Freeman already was set to have Friday off. He said he did not undergo X-ray scans Wednesday night. Roberts said he doesn't plan to promote an minor league players in the wake of Freeman's fall.

Ohtani went 2 for 4 with two RBIs, a run scored and a strikeout. Shortstop Mookie Betts also homered in the victory. Dodgers starter Eric Lauer allowed four hits and two runs, including one earned, over 6 1/3 innings to improve to 7-6 this season.

Freeman hit a team-high .306 with 15 home runs and 57 RBIs through 118 games this season.

The Dodgers (73-48), who were on a seven-game losing skid earlier this month, are now on a three-game winning streak. They hold an 8.5-game lead on the San Diego Padres (65-57), who sit in second place in the National League West.

The Dodgers will host the Milwaukee Brewers, who own the best record in the National League (74-47), at 10:10 p.m. EDT Thursday in Los Angeles.

title: How a roster loophole could solve Steelers' four-QB dilemma
description: By utilizing a practice squad loophole with veteran Mason Rudolph, the Pittsburgh Steelers can retain Will Howard and Drew Allar on the roster.
fullText:
As the Pittsburgh Steelers navigate a delicate quarterback puzzle behind starter Aaron Rodgers, head coach Mike McCarthy faces a classic 53-man roster crunch.

Carrying four quarterbacks: Rodgers, veteran Mason Rudolph, second-year passer Will Howard, and third-round rookie Drew Allar, is virtually unheard of in modern NFL roster construction. However, an intricate roster loophole involving Rudolph's status as a "vested veteran" could offer Pittsburgh an ideal strategic compromise to keep everyone.

Because Rudolph possesses at least four accrued NFL seasons, he is legally exempt from the league's waiver wire system if released. While non-vested young prospects like Howard or Allar would be exposed to waiver claims from 31 other teams, Rudolph immediately becomes an unrestricted free agent who can re-sign on his own terms.

During a recent segment on "PFT Live," NFL analyst Mike Florio broke down how Pittsburgh could exploit this procedural mechanism to protect its entire quarterback room:

"The veteran, the vested veteran gets cut, doesn't have to sign through waivers, hangs around, re-signs to the roster, signs to the practice squad. They could put Mason Rudolph on the practice squad, elevate him to the active roster, send him back down, do that a few weeks, and then do it all over again, release him from the roster," explained Florio.

Under NFL practice squad regulations, teams can elevate a veteran player up to three times per season without signing them to the active 53-man list. By executing a handshake agreement with Rudolph, Pittsburgh could temporarily release him at final roster cutdowns, stash him on the practice squad, and promote him on game days when needed.

This clever procedural maneuvering would allow the Steelers to retain their high-upside developmental assets on the 53-man roster while preserving Rudolph's essential veteran presence behind Rodgers without burning a valuable position spot. While reliant on mutual trust and personal flexibility, it provides Pittsburgh a unique mechanism to solve an otherwise difficult numbers game.

Watson, an undrafted free agent out of Memphis who ran an unofficial 4.39-second 40 at his pro day, made the Broncos' initial 53-man roster in 2024 and has bounced between the Broncos' active roster and practice squad since.

San Francisco hasn't announced any signings, but adding a body or two before Thursday's game would hardly be a surprise given the state of the room. It's also a reminder of how quickly joint practices can get complicated for the 49ers — in 2024, the team was forced to scrap its joint sessions with the Saints due to a bevy of injuries. title: This veteran to arrive at Newcastle United and be the positive influence needed?
description: Sometimes, experience is just as valuable as youth — and Newcastle United could be about to find that out. After weeks of uncertainty, ins and outs, rumours and endless speculation, things are finally beginning to settle down at Newcastle United.
fullText:
Sometimes, experience is just as valuable as youth — and Newcastle United could be about to find that out.

After weeks of uncertainty, ins and outs, rumours and endless speculation, things are finally beginning to settle down at Newcastle United.

There are fresh faces through the door, players returning from the World Cup, and a new manager and coaching staff putting the squad through its paces in La Manga, Spain.

From what I have seen of the early training sessions, the intensity is certainly there. Throw in temperatures of 30-plus degrees and the lads are going to know they have been working hard this week!

One thing that particularly pleased me was the apparent passion on show. Both the players and coaching staff looked fully engaged, and there seemed to be a real intensity about the sessions.

Of course, training is one thing — now we need to see that same attitude and commitment transferred onto the pitch when it really matters.

And then there is Pierre-Emile Højbjerg.

Reports linking the 31-year-old with a move to Newcastle have raised more than a few eyebrows, with a fee of around £10m-£15m being bandied about.

Personally, I don't see what all the fuss is about.

In fact, I think it could be a very sensible piece of business.

Højbjerg is a seasoned Premier League player with considerable experience, and at around £10m-£15m, he certainly wouldn't break the bank. More importantly, he could bring somethingNewcastle United will need in abundance — experience.

With several young players coming into the squad, having an experienced head in the dressing room could prove invaluable. Højbjerg knows the Premier League, understands the demands of playing at the highest level and, importantly, has been there before.

Sometimes the value of a player cannot simply be measured by goals, assists or statistics.

It can be measured by what happens around him.

The influence he has on younger players. The standards he sets in training. The calmness he brings when things aren't going according to plan. The voice in the dressing room when the pressure starts to build.

We have already seen how important that kind of experience can be.

Our noisy neighbours down the road benefited considerably from the addition of Granit Xhaka, while Newcastle themselves saw the impact Kieran Trippier made when he arrived at St James' Park.

Trippier wasn't just a footballer. He brought leadership, experience and standards — qualities that had a positive influence on those around him.

That kind of influence should never be underestimated.

So, while some supporters may question whether Højbjerg is the right age or whether the money would be better spent elsewhere, I would be more than happy to see him arrive on Tyneside.

Newcastle United have plenty of young talent. What they also need is the experience to help that talent flourish.

If Højbjerg can provide that, then perhaps this is one transfer we shouldn't be scoffing at.

Instead, we should be asking whether another experienced head could be exactly what this new-look Newcastle United needs.

description: The Vancouver Canucks should look into bringing in this veteran netminder, amid the likelihood of an experiment this upcoming season. The post Canucks Should Bring In This UFA Goalie Amid Demko Uncertainty appeared first on HEAVY.
fullText:
The Vancouver Canucks will likely need to conduct a bit of an experiment in 2026-27. The uncertainty surrounding Thatcher Demko's health could very well prompt the organization to carry three goalies.

Yes, the Canucks are rebuilding. But just because they're rebuilding it doesn't mean the team should throw a Zamboni driver out there if and when Demko goes down.

And that's the thing. There's no real telling when Demko could go down. The numbers have shown that Demko typically goes down after seven starts or so. Even if Demko remained fully healthy this season, the Canucks will have to be very careful with his workload.

That's why the Canucks will need a third goalie. The easiest and most cost-effective option is to call someone up from Abbotsford. That could mean Nikita Tolopilo getting a fair number of starts.

But would the organization be better off keeping Tolopilo in the press box when Demko plays? Or would the team be better served by Tolopilo getting regular reps in Abbotsford?

That's where a veteran goalie like Ingram comes into the mix. Ingram can hang around as the backup to Kevin Lankinen on the nights Demko doesn't even dress.

That's another thing. The Canucks, in order to manage Demko's workload, shouldn't even dress him on nights he doesn't play. That's why a tandem like Lankinen and Ingram on Demko's nights off would give the team a better chance to win and keep Demko healthy.

The most complex situation for the Canucks will be handling back-to-back sets this upcoming season. Since starting Demko in one leg and then having him back up the next night might be a bit much, Manny Malhotra can let Demko rest on consecutive nights, especially on the road.

Back-to-back sets away from Vancouver could prove especially challenging for Demko. So, rolling with Lankinen and Ingram on the road would help Demko avoid injury as much as possible.

At home, Demko could get one leg, with either Lankinen or Ingram starting the other. If such a rotation sounds weird, it looks to be the next big trend in the NHL, particularly with the season now moving to 84 games.

Canucks Could Have Interesting Comp for Petterson Trade

The Canucks already made a risky bet in signing Demko to the extension they did. Since no one will be taking the contract off their hands, the best thing the organization can do is just give Demko the best possible shot at succeeding.

That's why the Canucks can't suddenly get cheap with goaltending. The team will need to have stability in the crease, especially with a younger defense emerging around them. The last thing Vancouver should be looking at is something like an inexperienced goalie giving up three goals on five shots in the first period.

Having a solid netminder behind the likes of Zeev Buium and Tom Willander will be crucial in building their confidence as they grow into bona fide NHL defensemen. So, even if Ingram costs something like $3 million on a one-year deal, it's an investment the team must make in helping its young D core develop.

Fortunately, there's an interesting UFA option out there that could help add some more beef to the Bruins' lineup. That option is Logan Stanley.

The 6'7" 230-pound blueliner could very well give the Bruins a meaner edge heading into this season. That's something crucial when facing some of the more belligerent opponents like the Tampa Bay Lightning and Florida Panthers.

Adding Stanley should help solidify the bottom four, particularly with the departure of Andrew Peeke this summer. Peeke was mostly a defensive defenseman, something that all teams need to have in their bottom four.

Stanley brings that. He delivers decent if unspectacular play. His physicality is an asset, ensuring that the opposition remains honest.

The only question mark would be the terms of a deal for Stanley. The veteran blueliner is still 28 and likely looking for a multi-year deal. And that's just the thing. The Bruins might not be willing to commit beyond a one or two-year deal.

But there might be a way that the Bruins could bring Stanley in without breaking the bank.

The Bruins could take a shot on Stanley by signing him to a one-year, show-me deal. So, something along the lines of a $4 million cap hit, which might seem a bit onerous for a bottom-pairing defenseman, could make sense.

The deal could be part of a broader promise by the organization. If Stanley fits, the two sides could work out a contract extension. If he doesn't somehow fit in, he could be another NHL trade deadline piece to move.

Sure, the Bruins wouldn't get much for him at the deadline. But the club could allow Stanley to get another shot much like the Winnipeg Jets did this past season by sending him to the Buffalo Sabres.

Bruins Should Take Flyer on Hurricanes' Beleaguered Center

The prospect of rolling out Nikita Zadorov and Logan Stanley one after the other should be tantalizing to Bruins fans. The bruising, if not necessarily flashy play could help offset some of the apparent lack of offensive punch Boston shows.

The Bruins aren't built to win games by outscoring opponents. The game plan should once again focus on buying David Pastrnak enough time to bust games wide open.

And that's precisely what Stanley helps accomplish.

It's unclear if the Bruins would be willing to meet Stanley's contract demands. But if there's a way to work something out, the Bruins would be remiss if they didn't at least kick the tires on the hulking blueliner.

The Bruins need every edge they can get. And if it comes in a massive package, all the better. The Atlantic Division playoff race should be airtight. That's why having strong reinforcements could make a massive difference in 2026-27.

Veteran Democratic strategist James Carville told Fox News Digital Thursday there is only one unlikely scenario in which he would actually join the Republican Party.

Posed with a hypothetical where Republicans had the policies of former President Bill Clinton from the 1990s and the Democratic Party fully embraced socialism, Carville said, "That's a fantasy, OK, but, yeah, hypothetically, if I — hypothetically I could fly to the moon — it's about the same chance that that happens.

"Well, if the Democrats went crazy and the Republicans went sane, then I probably would be a Republican," he added. "But I don't see any evidence that there's any possibility that the latter could happen.

"I think it's more likely than not that the Democrats embrace sanity," Carville continued, saying the party's direction will be determined by Democratic primary voters.

Hasan Piker's Defense Of Hamas Having 'Right To Resist Militarily' Draws Condemnation From Human Rights Groups

In recent months, there has been a rising faction of far-left Democratic candidates in multiple states to the point Carville has suggested there be a schism to keep them out of power.

Hasan Piker, a self-described socialist streamer who campaigned with Democratic Michigan Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed, has emerged as a leading voice on the left as democratic socialists gain ground in elections across the country.

Piker is known for far-left rhetoric, including previously saying "America deserved 9/11." After widespread criticism, Piker said in an interview he "obviously" did not mean America deserved the attacks and defended the viral quote as a critique of U.S. foreign policy.

"I am not going to be in the same party with Hasan Piker," Carville said recently on Fox News' "The Sunday Briefing." "If he becomes a force in a Democratic Party, I'm out of here. I have no intention of ever being in the same political party with that guy."

Speaking to Fox News Digital on Thursday, Carville addressed what would happen if the socialist faction took over the Democratic Party.

"That probably would result in some kind of schism in the party," he reiterated. "I'm going to let Democratic voters determine the direction that party goes in, and if it goes in the direction — which I'm pretty confident it won't — but if it goes in that direction, then I'm going to be 82, OK, fine, go ahead, but not with me.

"Until Democratic voters choose the direction of the party, I'll try to do all I can to help them make the right choice, in my opinion."

John Fetterman Makes It 'Very Clear' That He's 'Not Going To Be A Republican' Despite Dem Backlash

Carville's threat to leave the Democratic Party has been mocked by its progressive wing.

"Now James Carville is talking about leaving the party," Piker said during a recent video appearance with El-Sayed. "We got [Pennsylvania Sen.] John Fetterman, James Carville fantasizing about leaving the party. I'm like, 'You're sweetening the deal.' That was really interesting."

Sen. Bernie Sanders, I-Vt., has also stood by Piker after Carville's warning.

"Well, that's not much of a choice," Sanders said of choosing between Piker and Carville. "If Mr. Carville doesn't want to be in my party, the party that I belong to, that Piker, that El-Sayed belongs to, he can start his own party."

fullText:
MILWAUKEE (AP) — With the Milwaukee Brewers' trade-deadline acquisition of veteran starter Dustin May, rookie right-hander Brandon Sproat became the odd man out of the rotation.

Sproat, who appeared in 21 games for Milwaukee, including 19 starts, was optioned Tuesday to Triple-A Nashville one day after another inconsistent start.

May, acquired from the Cardinals on Monday along with reliever JoJo Romero, is scheduled to start Thursday for Milwaukee in the series finale against Pittsburgh. Left-hander Kyle Harrison, on the injured list since July 9, also is scheduled to return and start Wednesday.

The 25-year-old Sproat, acquired from the Mets in the offseason trade for Freddy Peralta, is 3-7 with a 5.27 ERA for Milwaukee. He has not won in five starts since his last victory on June 30.

"I think you look at it at face value. It wasn't a foregone conclusion," Brewers manager Pat Murphy said before Tuesday's game. "It's really about what's best for the player and what's best for the team."

Sproat took the loss Monday in a 4-3 defeat in the series opener against the Pirates, allowing four runs on five hits in three-plus innings. He was removed after throwing consecutive wild pitches following a leadoff single in the fourth.

Sproat has struck out 100 in 95 2/3 innings with the Brewers. But he walked 48, hit nine batters and threw nine wild pitches.

"The free bases, the wild pitches, the walks, hit by pitches, has got to stop," Murphy said. "You can't pitch in the big leagues like that."

May was 5-7 with a 4.38 ERA in 21 starts with St. Louis, including 0-1 with a 4.62 ERA in six July starts.

The Brewers also optioned reliever Garrett Stallings to Nashville on Tuesday. In addition to getting Romero, Milwaukee also acquired reliever Antonio Senzatela from Colorado on Monday.

fullText:
MIAMI GARDENS — Confidence is a helluva thing. If you have it, you can move mountains. If you don’t have it, you’ll never move defensive tackles. This is what brings us around to Miami Dolphins right guard Jonah Savaiinaea, who had spirited battles with veteran defensive tackle Zach Sieler in Monday’s practice.

A year ago, as an out-of-position rookie left guard, Savaiinaea, the 2025 second-round pick, lost his confidence. Playing left guard in the NFL, instead of right guard, the position he played in college, resulted in Savaiinaea thinking instead of playing freely. It slowed him down. He became nervous. And he was way too hard on himself when he made mistakes. It was a weekslong downward spiral. A loss of confidence is a big reason why Savaiinaea was rated as one of the NFL’s worst guards by Pro Football Focus.

This season, Savaiianea is trying to rebuild his confidence. So are the the Dolphins. They’re on an all-out assault to bring Savaiinaea back from the dark side.

“I don’t want to hear any more about Jonah last year just because it’s over,” coach Jeff Hafley said. “Let’s judge Jonah on everything that he’s doing today, moving forward and see how he does.”

It remains to be seen whether this experiment will be successful. After all, this is the NFL. Every story doesn’t have a happy ending.

But Savaiinaea is personable, upbeat and positive so you hope he does well this season and beyond.

Still, this is an uphill battle.

Savaiinaea is viewed as the weak link on this offensive line. He’s not especially good against the run or pass, and he hasn’t displayed much physicality. The interesting thing is that the latter might be the biggest issue considering Hafley wants to have a physical team that’s strong in the trenches. You can teach run or pass blocking. It’s tougher to teach physicality.

This is where Savaiinaea’s mental reckoning could save his job as well as the Dolphins’ offensive line.

Savaiinaea is trying to make changes.

“It comes all in the mind,” he said. “I have the physical attributes to go out there and become a professional football player, but at the end of the day, it’s all about how you attack everything mentally. … I’m a different person as far as mentally.”

Savaiinaea actually started this process late last season.

“Towards the end of the year, I told myself, ‘I’m on myself too much, so why not take it easy on yourself?’ ” he said.

There are other things that Savaiinaea did to flip the script from last season.

He switched to No. 71, the number he wore in college and high school, ditching No. 72, which he wore last season.

“I want to bring that back and I want to get back to that kind of a reset mode and start to be myself again,” he said.

Savaiinaea did good work Monday, and has been fairly reliable through five days of training camp. He also did good work against defensive tackle Kenneth Grant on Monday in both 1 on 1s and 11 on 11s. Yes, there was a play in which defensive tackle Zeek Biggers knocked Savaiinaea on his backside in the final session of 11 on 11, but he didn’t threaten quarterback Malik Willis.

All things considered, Savaiinaea has shown improvement from a year ago. He attributes it mostly to a change between the ears.

“It’s how I approach my work,” he said. “Nothing changed because the side switched or the number switched. I don’t think so. I feel as if I approach this game like I’m coming there to move somebody out of there and protect Malik behind there, I feel like I’m going to be successful in this league.”

title: Could Tre'Davious White be a smart veteran addition for the Bucs?
description: Tre'Davious White remains unsigned and the Bucs could use more help in the secondary, so does a signing make sense?
fullText:
Outside of Zyon McCollum, Tampa Bay is relying on several young defensive backs to play meaningful snaps this season. While rookies and second-year players have flashed throughout camp, adding another proven veteran before Week 1 could still be a wise move. One player who stands out as a potential fit is former All-Pro cornerback Tre'Davious White.

White is no longer the player who was once considered one of the NFL's premier shutdown corners, but that doesn't mean he can't still provide value. After battling multiple major injuries over the last several seasons, including a torn ACL and Achilles injury, White has struggled to recapture the elite form that made him a two-time Pro Bowler. Those setbacks have understandably impacted both his availability and consistency. But that's exactly why he could be an affordable option this late in the offseason.

Todd Bowles has never been afraid to lean on experienced defensive backs, particularly those who have proven they can thrive in man coverage. While White may have lost a step athletically, his instincts, football IQ, and understanding of route concepts remain strengths. Veteran corners often make up for diminished speed with anticipation, positioning, and technique, and White has years of experience doing just that.

The Buccaneers also wouldn't need him to be the player he was in Buffalo.

Instead, he could serve as an experienced rotational corner, provide quality depth in case injuries strike, and mentor a young secondary that features several players still learning the real speed of the NFL game. There's little downside to bringing in a player with White's résumé on the right contract. If he returns to even a fraction of his previous Pro Bowl level, Tampa Bay could have one of the better value signings of the late offseason. If not, the financial commitment would likely be minimal.

White could help bridge the gap that is starters with experience and then the drop off to two sophomores still trying to find their footing in a complex defense, especially with Benjamin Morrison still struggling with injuries. Having the option to ease into younger corners instead of trial by fire allows for flexibility, one of Todd Bowles' biggest strengths. If Tampa Bay wants to fully resolve its woes of last season, White could be the final depth piece.

title: Bears Teammates Highlight Garrett Bradbury's Communication Skills in Camp
description: Following Drew Dalman’s retirement, veteran center Garrett Bradbury has impressed teammates with a seamless transition, providing the veteran leadership and vocal presence for the Chicago Bears' offensive line.
fullText:
The Chicago Bears finally had stable play from the center position last season.

Drew Dalman played every offensive snap and earned himself a Pro Bowl nod. After years of instability on the interior spot of the offensive line, there was finally consistency.

Dalman retired in March, and the Bears quickly traded for New England Patriots center Garrett Bradbury. The veteran offensive lineman has seven years of NFL experience and 105 starts to his name.

Although he's the new guy on the Bears' O-line, his teammates haven't noticed a drop off in the operation of head coach Ben Johnson's offense.

"I think we were all a little, you know, you don't know how it's going to go, especially when we lose somebody like Drew, who's, you know, kind of that captain of the offensive line there communication wise," Bears tight end Cole Kmet said. "But, I mean, with Garrett, it really has been flawless so far, and I know we haven't had pads on from a physicality standpoint, but, you know, you talked about communication in the walkthroughs that we've had, and in practice, things have been really clear, concise, and I feel like when I've been out there, especially in the run game and the pass pro, things have been really clear. And I think we've had great understanding with one another, so yeah, it's a good unit up front for sure."

Braxton Jones is currently in a competition for the starting left tackle position, but he's also noticed the cohesion he's felt with Bradbury playing with the starting unit.

"I mean, Garrett's jumped right in," Jones said. "He's, I mean, it's almost, it's weird like, you know, shoutout to Drew Dalman and everything he did, but, you know, Garrett jumped right in and has done a great job. It's like, you know, the same thing, their communication is great. And, you know, obvioulsy Garrett's a hell of a player himself, so it's been great and the continuity going forward. We're all a brotherhood. We all have a good time, but whe it's ready to, you know, get that work in, we're all getting that work in. So, it's just a great group to be around.

Caleb Williams is now playing with his third center in the last three years. The center and quarterback relationship is an important one for any offense. After last Wednesday's training camp practice, he mentioned that there was a slight miscommunication between the two.

Training camp is the time to address those miscues, as the Bears' quarterback is looking for perfection on game days.

Garrett doesn't have to be perfect -- or Dalman -- but he does need to provide a stable presence at the center position for this Bears offense to reach its next level.

The Chicago Cubs spent the days leading up to the MLB trade deadline searching for a starting pitcher capable of making a difference in October.

Chicago is acquiring veteran right-hander Kevin Gausman in a trade with the Toronto Blue Jays, ESPN’s Jeff Passan reported Sunday. Ken Rosenthal of The Athletic and Mitch Bannon were first to report the agreement.

The players heading back to Toronto were not immediately revealed.

The move gives the Cubs an experienced arm for the stretch run after the organization made upgrading its rotation a deadline priority. Although Gausman has not produced his best numbers this season, his track record and ability to miss bats make him a potentially significant addition.

Gausman owns a 5-10 record with a 4.38 ERA across 23 starts this season. He has recorded 127 strikeouts and 36 walks over 127.1 innings while posting a 1.29 WHIP.

Those numbers may not immediately jump off the page, but Gausman has shown encouraging signs recently. The 35-year-old allowed only one earned run over 5.2 innings against the St. Louis Cardinals on Saturday. He surrendered nine hits but avoided major damage, issuing one walk and striking out four in Toronto’s 5-1 victory.

Gausman also worked six innings against the Boston Red Sox in his previous start, allowing three earned runs while striking out six. Across his final two appearances for the Blue Jays, he recorded a 3.09 ERA with 10 strikeouts and only two walks in 11.2 innings. He joins Chicago with 385 major league appearances, including 345 starts. The two-time All-Star has compiled 2,081 strikeouts across more than 2,000 career innings while pitching for the Baltimore Orioles, Atlanta Braves, Cincinnati Reds, San Francisco Giants and Blue Jays.

The Cubs entered Sunday with a 61-51 record after a 2-1 loss to the New York Yankees. They remain firmly in the National League playoff race but needed another reliable starter to strengthen their chances of making a deep run.

Gausman gives Chicago a veteran who can absorb innings, generate strikeouts and potentially start an important postseason game.

He also arrives with another year remaining on the five-year, $110 million contract he signed with Toronto before the 2022 season. Gausman is scheduled to earn $23 million in 2027, meaning this is more than a short-term rental for the Cubs.

For the Blue Jays, the trade signals a different direction. Toronto fell to 52-60 with Saturday’s loss to St. Louis and entered Sunday 13.5 games behind the Tampa Bay Rays in the American League East.

Rather than holding onto Gausman for another season, the Blue Jays elected to move one of their most accomplished starters and add to their future.

The full return will ultimately help determine how the trade is evaluated. For now, however, the immediate message is clear: The Cubs believe they can contend this season, and they have added one of the most established pitchers available to help them do it.

title: Braves reportedly acquire SP Tyler Mahle from Giants, further boosting pitching depth

fullText:
